# About this comparison

This vignette compares `empirical_fit = "mixture"` with the older
`empirical_fit = "central"` on the HAP1 CRISPR-Cas9 dropout screen shipped
with ScreenR. We first inspect guide-level before/after ratios, then compare
the fitted nulls and their p-values, and finally call depleted genes at day
18 against T0. See [Choosing the reference](Empirical_null.html) for the
gene-level test and [Tutorial 4](Tutorial_4_CRISPR_screens.html) for the screen.

**Status:** the mixture method is experimental, opt-in, and not the default.
Its FDR calibration gate has not passed yet. This dataset comparison is a
diagnostic example; it does not establish FDR control or justify changing the
default fit.

```{r packages, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(ScreenR)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r reference-genes}
data(hap1_count_table)
data(hap1_annotation_table)
data(hart_reference_genes)
essential <- hart_reference_genes$Gene[
    hart_reference_genes$Class == "core essential"]
nonessential <- hart_reference_genes$Gene[
    hart_reference_genes$Class == "non-essential"]
controls <- c("EGFP", "LacZ", "luciferase")
class_of <- function(gene) {
    case_when(
        gene %in% essential ~ "Core essential",
        gene %in% nonessential ~ "Non-essential",
        gene %in% controls ~ "Control",
        TRUE ~ "Unclassified"
    )
}
```

The Hart reference lists are used only to evaluate the results, not to fit
either null. The annotated control targets are shown separately: their
behaviour need not match that of guides cutting non-essential human genes.
Unclassified genes have no label in these reference lists, so calling one
does not by itself imply a false positive.

# Before/after ratios and asymmetry

We follow the ratio construction used by Imkeller et al. (2020),
[gscreend, Genome Biology 21:53](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-020-1939-1):
scale each T18 replicate to the total count at T0, add a pseudocount of one,
and calculate `log2((T18_scaled + 1) / (T0 + 1))`. Negative ratios indicate
depletion. This reproduces the descriptive ratio analysis on HAP1; the
gscreend statistical test is not run here.

```{r guide-ratios}
counts <- hap1_count_table
t0 <- as.numeric(counts$T0)
replicates <- c("T18_A", "T18_B", "T18_C")
ratios <- sapply(replicates, function(replicate) {
    after <- as.numeric(counts[[replicate]])
    scaled <- after * sum(t0) / sum(after)
    log2((scaled + 1) / (t0 + 1))
})
gene <- hap1_annotation_table$Gene[
    match(counts$Barcode, hap1_annotation_table$Barcode)]
guide_table <- data.frame(
    Barcode = counts$Barcode, Gene = gene, Class = class_of(gene),
    T0 = t0, ratios, LFC = rowMeans(ratios)
)
guide_table <- guide_table[t0 > 0, ]
ratio_long <- pivot_longer(guide_table, all_of(replicates),
    names_to = "Replicate", values_to = "Ratio")
null_ratios <- filter(ratio_long, Class %in% c("Non-essential", "Control"))
```

Scaling uses all guides before removing those with zero T0 counts. There are
`r nrow(guide_table)` guides with positive T0 counts, including
`r sum(guide_table$Class == "Non-essential")` non-essential and
`r sum(guide_table$Class == "Control")` control guides. Positive T0 is
required for the abundance covariate below.

```{r ratio-histograms, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(null_ratios, aes(Ratio, fill = Class)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 80,
        alpha = 0.6, position = "identity") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~Replicate) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5, 3)) +
    labs(x = "log2 before/after ratio (T18 / T0)", y = "Density") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The raw tail fractions beyond -1 and +1 combine location and shape. We also
subtract the median separately within each class and replicate before
counting the tails, to distinguish a location shift from asymmetry. Skewness
is `mean((Ratio - mean(Ratio))^3) / sd(Ratio)^3`; negative values indicate a
longer left tail. It is unchanged by median centring.

```{r ratio-tail-fractions}
ratio_summary <- null_ratios %>%
    group_by(Class, Replicate) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), Median = median(Ratio),
        Skewness = mean((Ratio - mean(Ratio))^3) / sd(Ratio)^3,
        .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(ratio_summary, digits = 3)

tail_summary <- null_ratios %>%
    group_by(Class, Replicate) %>%
    mutate(Centred = Ratio - median(Ratio)) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(Ratio, Centred), names_to = "Scale", values_to = "Value") %>%
    group_by(Class, Replicate, Scale) %>%
    summarise(`Below -1` = mean(Value < -1),
        `Above +1` = mean(Value > 1),
        `Left / right` = `Below -1` / `Above +1`, .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(tail_summary, digits = 3)
```

For the spread analysis, we average the replicate log ratios for each guide
and divide the non-essential guides into T0 abundance deciles. The table
reports the median T0 count, median ratio, standard deviation and raw tail
fractions in each decile. This checks whether a single spread is adequate
across the abundance range.

```{r abundance-deciles}
strata <- guide_table %>%
    filter(Class == "Non-essential") %>%
    mutate(Decile = ntile(T0, 10)) %>%
    group_by(Decile) %>%
    summarise(T0_median = median(T0), LFC_median = median(LFC),
        LFC_sd = sd(LFC), below_minus1 = mean(LFC < -1),
        above_plus1 = mean(LFC > 1), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(strata, digits = 3)
ggplot(strata, aes(factor(Decile), LFC_sd)) +
    geom_col(fill = "grey50") +
    labs(x = "T0 abundance decile (non-essential guides)",
        y = "SD of mean log2 ratio")
```

# Fitting the guide-level null

Here both fits use the mean log ratio of **all** retained guides. The central
fit estimates one normal distribution around the mode. The mixture fits a
skew-normal neutral component and normal depleted and enriched components.
The neutral location and log scale depend linearly on
`x = log2(T0) - mean(log2(T0))`, with a constant shape parameter `alpha`.
Its neutral CDF uses `sn::psn()` and its density uses `sn::dsn()`.
Amendment A4 fits a deterministic profile in `alpha`: a grid of step 0.25
starts at [-4, 4] and extends toward [-10, 10] if needed. At each shape the
other ten parameters are optimized using continuation and deterministic
starts; the best grid point is refined to obtain `alpha_hat`. The 95%
profile interval contains shapes whose log likelihood is within
`qchisq(0.95, 1) / 2` of the maximum. Default p-values use a conservative
alpha envelope: the largest directional neutral tail probability over the
grid points within that interval and the refined MLE. The MLE-only p-values
are retained for diagnostics. Thus the plotted density is at `alpha_hat`,
while p-values account for uncertainty in shape. The normal alternatives are wider
than the neutral component and centred at least three neutral standard
deviations from its mean. This is a different model and fitting procedure
from gscreend, although both allow a skew-normal neutral distribution.

`mixture_null_fit()`, `mixture_null_cdf()` and `mixture_null_density()` are
internal functions, accessed
with `ScreenR:::` for this diagnostic example. The central helper is internal
too. These helpers are not a stable public interface; the public gene-level
interface is demonstrated in the next section.

```{r guide-fits}
x_raw <- log2(guide_table$T0)
x <- x_raw - mean(x_raw)
central <- ScreenR:::fit_null_central(guide_table$LFC)
mixture <- ScreenR:::mixture_null_fit(guide_table$LFC, x)
guide_table$p_central <- pnorm(guide_table$LFC,
    mean = central[["mean"]], sd = central[["sd"]])
guide_table$p_mixture <- ScreenR:::mixture_null_cdf(
    mixture, guide_table$LFC, x)
central
mixture$weights
mixture$theta
data.frame(alpha_hat = mixture$alpha_hat,
    alpha_ci_lower = mixture$alpha_ci[["lower"]],
    alpha_ci_upper = mixture$alpha_ci[["upper"]],
    convergence = mixture$convergence, fallback = mixture$fallback,
    at_bound = paste(mixture$at_bound, collapse = ", "))
```

The following curves average each mixture component over the observed T0
covariates. Component densities include their fitted mixture weights, so
their areas are their proportions of all guides. The central curve has unit
area. The neutral CDF used for p-values is unweighted: a depleted-tail
p-value is the probability below the observed ratio under the neutral
component, not the probability of membership in that component.

```{r guide-density, fig.height = 5}
grid <- seq(-6, 3, length.out = 600)
plot_x <- unique(x)
plot_weights <- tabulate(match(x, plot_x)) / length(x)
component <- function(which) {
    vapply(grid, function(value) {
        sum(plot_weights * ScreenR:::mixture_null_density(mixture,
            rep(value, length(plot_x)), plot_x, component = which))
    }, numeric(1))
}
curves <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(t = grid, density = dnorm(grid, central[["mean"]],
        central[["sd"]]), Fit = "Central: normal"),
    data.frame(t = grid, density = component("null"),
        Fit = "Mixture: neutral (weighted)"),
    data.frame(t = grid, density = component("down"),
        Fit = "Mixture: depleted"),
    data.frame(t = grid, density = component("up"),
        Fit = "Mixture: enriched")
)
ggplot(guide_table, aes(LFC)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 120,
        fill = "grey80", colour = "grey60") +
    geom_line(data = curves, aes(t, density, colour = Fit), linewidth = 0.8) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-6, 3)) +
    labs(x = "Mean log2 before/after ratio", y = "Density", colour = NULL,
        subtitle = "Density at alpha_hat; p-values use the conservative alpha envelope") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

These guide-level fits use the same guides for fitting and evaluation, so
their p-values are descriptive. We inspect both tails for the non-essential
guides, with controls alongside them. MLE-only p-values would be uniform
under a correctly specified continuous null. The conservative envelope can
increase the lower-tail p-values; it need not be uniform, and its two
directional tails need not sum to one.

```{r guide-p-values, fig.height = 4}
guide_p <- guide_table %>%
    filter(Class %in% c("Non-essential", "Control")) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(p_central, p_mixture), names_to = "Fit", values_to = "p") %>%
    mutate(Fit = recode(Fit, p_central = "Central", p_mixture = "Mixture"))
guide_calibration <- guide_p %>%
    group_by(Class, Fit) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), `p < 0.01` = mean(p < 0.01),
        `p < 0.05` = mean(p < 0.05), `p > 0.95` = mean(p > 0.95),
        `p > 0.99` = mean(p > 0.99), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(guide_calibration, digits = 3)
ggplot(filter(guide_p, Class == "Non-essential"), aes(p)) +
    geom_histogram(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.05), fill = "grey50") +
    geom_hline(data = count(filter(guide_p, Class == "Non-essential"), Fit),
        aes(yintercept = n / 20), linetype = 2, colour = "red") +
    facet_wrap(~Fit) +
    labs(x = "Depletion p-value of non-essential guides", y = "Guides",
        subtitle = "Dashed line: expected count per bin under uniform p-values")
```

# Calling depleted genes

The public test uses barcode Z-scores from `compute_metrics()`, rather than
the descriptive count ratios above. We normalize the supplied count table
and compare day 18 with T0. The gene statistic is the mean barcode Z-score,
standardized using the barcode median and MAD and the number of guides per
gene. Genes need at least three guides, the default `min_barcodes`.

```{r gene-metrics, message = FALSE}
samples <- data.frame(
    Sample = colnames(hap1_count_table)[-1],
    Day = c("T0", "T3", "T3", "T3", "T18", "T18", "T18"),
    Treatment = "Untreated"
)
hap1 <- create_screenr_object(
    table = hap1_count_table, annotation = hap1_annotation_table,
    groups = factor(samples$Day, levels = c("T0", "T3", "T18")),
    sample_table = samples
)
hap1 <- normalize_data(remove_all_zero_row(hap1))
day18 <- compute_metrics(hap1, control = "T0", treatment = "T18",
    condition_column = "Day")
```

For the gene-level mixture the covariate is centred **log number of guides
per gene**, not T0 abundance. With five folds and seed 2017, each gene's
p-value comes from a fit on the other folds. BH adjustment is then applied
once across all tested genes. `fdr = 1` retains every tested gene so that
non-essential p-values can be evaluated as well as hits.

```{r gene-tests}
# Derive the MLE-only comparison without fitting the same folds again.
gene_results <- lapply(c("central", "mixture"), function(fit) {
    find_gene_zscore_hit(day18, reference = "empirical",
        empirical_fit = fit, direction = "Down", fdr = 1,
        fdr_method = "BH", seed = 2017, n_folds = 5)
})
names(gene_results) <- c("central", "mixture conservative")
with_mle_pvalues <- function(results) {
    mle <- results[["mixture conservative"]]
    null <- attr(mle, "null")
    mle$PValue <- null$p_down_mle[match(mle$Gene, null$genes)]
    mle$FDR <- p.adjust(mle$PValue, method = "BH")
    list(central = results$central, `mixture MLE-only` = mle,
        `mixture conservative` = results[["mixture conservative"]])
}
gene_results <- with_mle_pvalues(gene_results)
evaluate_genes <- function(result) {
    class <- class_of(result$Gene)
    hit <- result$FDR <= 0.05
    data.frame(Tested = nrow(result), Hits = sum(hit),
        `Core essentials found` = sum(hit & class == "Core essential"),
        `Non-essentials called` = sum(hit & class == "Non-essential"),
        `NE p < 0.05` = mean(result$PValue[class == "Non-essential"] < 0.05),
        `Unclassified called` = sum(hit & class == "Unclassified"),
        check.names = FALSE)
}
gene_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(gene_results, evaluate_genes), .id = "Fit")
knitr::kable(gene_summary, digits = 3)
```

Among the tested genes, there are
`r sum(gene_results$central$Gene %in% essential)` core essentials and
`r sum(gene_results$central$Gene %in% nonessential)` non-essentials. At a
nominal BH FDR threshold of 0.05, the central fit calls
`r gene_summary$Hits[gene_summary$Fit == "central"]` genes and the mixture
conservative envelope calls
`r gene_summary$Hits[gene_summary$Fit == "mixture conservative"]`.
The MLE-only mixture calls
`r gene_summary$Hits[gene_summary$Fit == "mixture MLE-only"]`. The non-essential
p-value fraction is a marginal calibration diagnostic, not an estimate of
the FDR among all hits: the reference lists do not classify every gene.

```{r gene-null-central}
plot_empirical_null(day18, empirical_fit = "central",
    direction = "Down", seed = 2017, n_folds = 5) +
    ggtitle("Gene statistic: central empirical null")
```

```{r gene-null-mixture}
ScreenR:::plot_mixture_null(gene_results[["mixture conservative"]],
    attr(gene_results[["mixture conservative"]], "null"), bins = 60) +
    ggtitle("Gene statistic: mixture empirical null")
```

The mixture plot averages the neutral density over held-out covariates,
weighted by each fold's fitted neutral proportion. The central plot uses a
single fitted normal density. Inspect the diagnostics as well as the curves:
convergence does not establish calibration, and a parameter at a bound can
signal that a component is weakly identified.

```{r fold-diagnostics}
gene_null <- attr(gene_results[["mixture conservative"]], "null")
per_fold <- gene_null$diagnostics$per_fold
knitr::kable(per_fold[, c("fold", "n_train", "n_test", "convergence",
    "fallback", "starts_converged", "at_bound")])
knitr::kable(per_fold[, c("fold", "mu0", "s", "alpha_hat",
    "alpha_ci_lower", "alpha_ci_upper", "pi0", "pi_down", "pi_up")],
    digits = 4)
knitr::kable(data.frame(Parameter = names(gene_null$diagnostics$spread),
    `Across-fold SD` = unname(gene_null$diagnostics$spread),
    check.names = FALSE), digits = 4)
```

Here `mu0` is the skew-normal location at centred covariate zero, `s` its log
scale, `alpha_hat` its fitted shape, `alpha_ci_lower` and
`alpha_ci_upper` its 95% profile interval endpoints, and `pi0`, `pi_down` and `pi_up` the component
proportions. With nonzero shape, location and scale differ from the neutral
mean and standard deviation. There
are `r sum(per_fold$convergence == 0)` converged folds,
`r sum(per_fold$fallback)` fallback fits and
`r sum(nzchar(per_fold$at_bound))` folds with a parameter at a bound. These
checks and the reference-gene results describe this screen only; the FDR
calibration gate still needs to pass before the method can be treated as
validated.

# One replicate versus three

We now repeat the comparison with each T18 replicate on its own. The first
table uses the same non-essential guides with positive T0 counts for all
inputs. `Mean of 3` is the mean of the three **log ratios** used in the
guide analysis above. The tail fractions are calculated after subtracting
the median of each input.

```{r single-replicate-ratios}
ratio_inputs <- c(setNames(lapply(replicates, function(replicate) {
    guide_table[[replicate]]
}), replicates), list(`Mean of 3` = guide_table$LFC))
single_spread <- bind_rows(lapply(ratio_inputs, function(ratio) {
    values <- ratio[guide_table$Class == "Non-essential"]
    centred <- values - median(values)
    data.frame(n = length(values), SD = sd(values),
        `Below median - 1` = mean(centred < -1),
        `Above median + 1` = mean(centred > 1),
        Skewness = mean((values - mean(values))^3) / sd(values)^3,
        check.names = FALSE)
}), .id = "Input")
knitr::kable(single_spread, digits = 3)
```

The SDs of the individual replicates are
`r paste(sprintf("%.3f", single_spread$SD[single_spread$Input != "Mean of 3"]), collapse = ", ")`,
compared with
`r sprintf("%.3f", single_spread$SD[single_spread$Input == "Mean of 3"])`
for their mean. Averaging can reduce spread while leaving asymmetry, so we
also inspect calibration after fitting each input separately.

```{r single-replicate-guide-calibration}
guide_fits <- lapply(ratio_inputs[replicates], function(ratio) {
    list(central = ScreenR:::fit_null_central(ratio),
        mixture = ScreenR:::mixture_null_fit(ratio, x))
})
guide_fits[["Mean of 3"]] <- list(central = central, mixture = mixture)
single_guide_calibration <- bind_rows(lapply(names(ratio_inputs), function(input) {
    ratio <- ratio_inputs[[input]]
    fits <- guide_fits[[input]]
    p_values <- list(
        central = pnorm(ratio, fits$central[["mean"]], fits$central[["sd"]]),
        mixture = ScreenR:::mixture_null_cdf(fits$mixture, ratio, x)
    )
    bind_rows(lapply(p_values, function(p) {
        p <- p[guide_table$Class == "Non-essential"]
        data.frame(`p < 0.01` = mean(p < 0.01),
            `p < 0.05` = mean(p < 0.05), check.names = FALSE)
    }), .id = "Fit") %>% mutate(Input = input, .before = 1)
}))
knitr::kable(single_guide_calibration, digits = 3)
```

For the gene comparison we subset the normalized ScreenR object to T0 and
one T18 replicate before calling `compute_metrics()`. Subsetting retains the
CPM effective library sizes; the other T18 replicates cannot contribute to
that contrast. The three-replicate gene analysis averages normalized counts
**before** taking the log ratio, as `compute_metrics()` normally does. It
therefore differs from averaging log ratios in the descriptive guide
analysis. This Z-score workflow does not estimate replicate variability;
the comparison shows the effect of averaging counts on its gene statistics.

```{r single-replicate-gene-calibration, message = FALSE}
single_gene_results <- lapply(replicates, function(replicate) {
    pair <- hap1[, c("T0", replicate)]
    metrics <- compute_metrics(pair, control = "T0", treatment = "T18",
        condition_column = "Day")
    fits <- lapply(c("central", "mixture"), function(fit) {
        find_gene_zscore_hit(metrics, reference = "empirical",
            empirical_fit = fit, direction = "Down", fdr = 1,
            fdr_method = "BH", seed = 2017, n_folds = 5)
    })
    with_mle_pvalues(setNames(fits, c("central", "mixture conservative")))
})
names(single_gene_results) <- replicates
single_gene_results[["Mean of 3"]] <- gene_results
single_gene_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(single_gene_results, function(results) {
    bind_rows(lapply(results, evaluate_genes), .id = "Fit")
}), .id = "Input")
knitr::kable(single_gene_summary, digits = 3)
```

Each row uses the same nominal BH FDR threshold of 0.05 and evaluates the
same Hart reference lists. The non-essential p-value fractions and false
calls should be considered alongside essential recovery; a larger hit list
alone does not establish better calibration. Neither the single-replicate
comparison nor averaging replaces the pending FDR calibration gate.

```{r all-fold-profiles}
all_folds <- bind_rows(lapply(single_gene_results, function(results) {
    attr(results[["mixture conservative"]], "null")$diagnostics$per_fold
}), .id = "Input")
knitr::kable(all_folds[, c("Input", "fold", "alpha_hat", "alpha_ci_lower",
    "alpha_ci_upper", "pi0", "convergence", "fallback")], digits = 3)
```

At the same statistic (-2.5) and centred covariate zero, we compare the
largest and smallest depletion p-values across the five training fits.
This isolates fold disagreement from differences between genes or covariates.

```{r fold-tail-stability}
fold_stability <- bind_rows(lapply(c("Mean of 3", "T18_B"), function(input) {
    null <- attr(single_gene_results[[input]][["mixture conservative"]], "null")
    mle <- vapply(null$fits, function(fit) {
        ScreenR:::mixture_null_cdf(fit, -2.5, 0, conservative = FALSE)
    }, numeric(1))
    conservative <- vapply(null$fits, function(fit) {
        ScreenR:::mixture_null_cdf(fit, -2.5, 0, conservative = TRUE)
    }, numeric(1))
    data.frame(Input = input, MLE_spread = max(mle) / min(mle),
        Conservative_spread = max(conservative) / min(conservative),
        Alpha_span = diff(range(vapply(null$fits, function(fit) fit$alpha_hat,
            numeric(1)))))
}))
knitr::kable(fold_stability, digits = 2)
```

`r if (any(fold_stability$Alpha_span > 0.5)) "Fold disagreement in the fitted shape remains." else "The fitted shapes agree closely across folds."`
For Mean of 3, the envelope changes the fold-to-fold p-value spread from
`r sprintf("%.1f", fold_stability$MLE_spread[1])` times to
`r sprintf("%.1f", fold_stability$Conservative_spread[1])` times, a
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (1 - fold_stability$Conservative_spread[1] / fold_stability$MLE_spread[1]))`%
reduction in the largest/smallest ratio. For T18_B it changes from
`r sprintf("%.1f", fold_stability$MLE_spread[2])` times to
`r sprintf("%.1f", fold_stability$Conservative_spread[2])` times, a
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (1 - fold_stability$Conservative_spread[2] / fold_stability$MLE_spread[2]))`%
reduction. The envelope reduces the consequence of weak shape identification;
it does not eliminate uncertainty or replace the pending calibration gate.

# Literature

* Imkeller K, Ambrosi G, Boutros M, Huber W (2020). gscreend: modelling
  asymmetric count ratios in CRISPR screens to decrease experiment size and
  improve phenotype detection. Genome Biology 21:53.
  [doi:10.1186/s13059-020-1939-1](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-020-1939-1).
* Hart T, Tong AHY, Chan K et al. (2017). Evaluation and design of
  genome-wide CRISPR/SpCas9 knockout screens. G3 7:2719-2727.
* Hart T, Brown KR, Sircoulomb F, Rottapel R, Moffat J (2014). Measuring
  error rates in genomic perturbation screens: gold standards for human
  functional genomics. Molecular Systems Biology 10:733.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
